newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. T-BOND GAINS IN TOKYO ON INVESTOR BUYING.
newsitem.headline: U.S. T-BOND GAINS IN TOKYO ON INVESTOR BUYING.

text.p: The key 30-year U.S. Treasury bond price firmed modestly in Tokyo on Monday morning due to buying by Japanese investors after a steep fall on Friday.
The dollar's partial recovery against the yen in Tokyo after a nearly four yen fall on Friday overseas also encouraged some buying, dealers said.
"Investors are willing to buy the bond if the dollar is firmly supported above 115 yen," said a U.S. bank dealer.
The dollar was standing at 115.36/41 yen at 0204 GMT. The key 30-year bond due 2027 was at around 96-26/32 or a 6.375 percent yield, up from the 96-20/32 New York close on Friday.

The yield of the 30-year Treasury bond rose to 6.66 percent at one point in New York trade, its highest since July 2. Concern about a strong retail sales report due out this week and the dollar's weakness contributed to bearish sentiment.
Traders said Friday's losses were mainly driven by technical factors amid a lack of significant change in U.S. economic fundamentals.

"The market saw the recent rallies as overdone and then corrected them with internal force," said a dealer at a U.S. securities houses. He said the market would be shaky for a while and further falls in prices were possible.

Falls in the U.S. stock and corporate bond markets prompted investors to sell liquid Treasuries for hedging purposes and this caused a sell-off in the Treasury market, said a dealer at a Japanese brokerage house.
U.S. operators had switched part of their investments to U.S. corporate bonds with higher returns when the key 30-year bond yield fell close to 6.25 percent, he added.
Dealers said they were focusing on a slew of U.S. inflation data due out this week, but many do not expect the data to lead to a quick change in monetary policy by the Federal Reserve.
